results.q: What happens when an RTU frame has a bad CRC?
answer: Invalid data is caught in _modbus_rtu_check_integrity() (src/modbus-rtu.c:387): it checks `crc_calculated != crc_received`, and when that is true it checks `ctx->debug` (line 388); if true it calls fprintf() and checks `ctx->error_recovery & MODBUS_ERROR_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL` (MODBUS_ERROR_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL = 4) (line 395); if true it calls _modbus_rtu_flush() and calls __error() (line 398) and returns `-1` (line 399) and returns `-1`, so the rest of _modbus_rtu_check_integrity() is skipped.

_modbus_rtu_flush() sets `modbus_rtu_t *ctx_rtu = ctx->backend_data` (line 1211); then it sets `ctx_rtu->w_ser.n_bytes = 0` (line 1212); then it calls PurgeComm() (line 1213); then it returns `(PurgeComm(ctx_rtu->w_ser.fd, PURGE_RXCLEAR) == FALSE)` (line 1213).

Consequence: win32_ser_select() checks `ReadFile(ws->fd, &ws->buf, max_len, &ws->n_bytes, NULL)` (src/modbus-rtu.c:208); `ReadFile(ws->fd, &ws->buf, max_len, &ws->n_bytes, NULL)` depends on runtime values, so it may return early and may call ReadFile().

These parts of the code look most relevant: compute_meta_length_after_function() (function, src/modbus.c:280); compute_response_length_from_request() (function, src/modbus.c:133); compute_data_length_after_meta() (function, src/modbus.c:319); table_crc_hi (global variable, src/modbus-rtu.c:33); crc16() (function, src/modbus-rtu.c:119); table_crc_lo (global variable, src/modbus-rtu.c:55).
compute_meta_length_after_function() (src/modbus.c:280) — Computes the length to read after the function received.

Step by step, it checks `msg_type == MSG_INDICATION` (MSG_INDICATION = 0) (line 284); then it checks `function <= MODBUS_FC_WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER` (line 285); then it checks `function == MODBUS_FC_WRITE_MULTIPLE_COILS || function == MODBUS_FC_WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS` (line 287); then it checks `function == MODBUS_FC_MASK_WRITE_REGISTER` (line 290); then it checks `function == MODBUS_FC_WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS` (line 292); then it chooses a case based on `function` (line 300); then it returns `length` (line 315).

It is called by _modbus_rtu_send_msg_pre() at src/modbus-rtu.c:143 with (`req`, `req_length`); _modbus_rtu_check_integrity() at src/modbus-rtu.c:383 with (`msg`, `msg_length - 2`). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → modbus_write_and_read_registers() → send_msg() → _modbus_rtu_send_msg_pre() → crc16().

It is called by _modbus_receive_msg() (through the dispatch table _modbus_backend.check_integrity) at src/modbus.c:546 (_modbus_rtu_check_integrity() is listed in the table _modbus_rtu_backend at src/modbus-rtu.c:1286) with (`ctx`, `msg`, `msg_length`) — `int msg_length = 0` (line 372), only when `!ctx->backend->is_connected(ctx)` is false, only when `ctx->s < 0 || ctx->s >= FD_SETSIZE` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → modbus_write_and_read_registers() → _modbus_receive_msg() → _modbus_rtu_check_integrity().

results.q: What happens when the slave does not answer before the response timeout?
answer: Losing the data is detected in _modbus_receive_msg() (src/modbus.c:530), which checks `length_to_read > 0 && (ctx->byte_timeout.tv_sec > 0 || ctx->byte_timeout.tv_usec > 0)`.
When that happens it sets `tv.tv_sec = ctx->byte_timeout.tv_sec`; sets `tv.tv_usec = ctx->byte_timeout.tv_usec`.

Note that this only triggers when all of these hold: `length_to_read > 0`; `(ctx->byte_timeout.tv_sec > 0 || ctx->byte_timeout.tv_usec > 0)`. For example, if no data was ever received, `length_to_read > 0` is false and this path is not taken.

results.q: What does modbus_new_rtu do when the baud rate is not positive?
answer: modbus_new_rtu() (src/modbus-rtu.c:1298) — clang-format on.

Step by step, it checks `device == NULL || *device == 0` (line 1305); if true it calls fprintf(), __error() and returns `NULL` straight away; then it checks `baud <= 0` (line 1312); if true it calls fprintf(), __error() and returns `NULL` straight away; then it checks `data_bit < 5 || data_bit > 8` (line 1319); if true it calls fprintf(), __error() and returns `NULL` straight away; then it checks `stop_bit != 1 && stop_bit != 2` (line 1326); if true it calls fprintf(), __error() and returns `NULL` straight away; then it calls malloc() and stores the result in `ctx` (line 1332); then it checks `ctx == NULL` (line 1333); if true it returns `NULL` straight away; then it calls _modbus_init_common() (line 1337); then it sets `ctx->backend = &_modbus_rtu_backend` (line 1338); then it calls malloc() and stores the result in `ctx->backend_data` (line 1339); then it checks `ctx->backend_data == NULL` (line 1340); if true it calls modbus_free(), __error() and returns `NULL` straight away; ….

It is called by main() at tests/bandwidth-client.c:76, only when `use_backend == TCP` is false (TCP = 0); main() at tests/bandwidth-server-one.c:56, only when `use_backend == TCP` is false (TCP = 0); main() at tests/unit-test-client.c:125, only when `use_backend == TCP` is false (TCP = 0), only when `use_backend == TCP_PI` is false (TCP_PI = 1); main() at tests/unit-test-client.c:793, only when `ctx == NULL` is false, only when `modbus_connect(ctx) == -1` is false, only when `test_server(ctx, use_backend) == -1` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → modbus_new_rtu().

The values it updates are used later by _modbus_rtu_send() (uses _modbus.backend_data, win32_ser.fd); _modbus_rtu_connect() (uses _modbus.backend_data, win32_ser.fd); _modbus_rtu_is_connected() (uses _modbus.backend_data, win32_ser.fd); _modbus_rtu_close() (uses _modbus.backend_data, win32_ser.fd).

results.q: Where is the slave address stored?
answer: Related values are also set here: `sft.slave = raw_req[0]` in modbus_send_raw_request_tid() (src/modbus.c:252); `sft.slave = slave` in modbus_reply() (src/modbus.c:844); `sft.slave = slave` in modbus_reply_exception() (src/modbus.c:1285); `sft.slave = backend_req[0]` in modbus_proxy() (src/modbus.c:1362); `check_sft.slave = sft.slave` in modbus_proxy() (src/modbus.c:1397); `sft.slave = backend_rsp[backend_header_length - 1]` in modbus_proxy() (src/modbus.c:1428).

results.q: What happens when a request asks for an illegal data address?
answer: This is handled in _modbus_rtu_pre_check_confirmation() (src/modbus-rtu.c:360): it checks `req[0] != rsp[0] && req[0] != MODBUS_BROADCAST_ADDRESS`, and when that is true it checks `ctx->debug` (line 361); if true it calls fprintf() and calls __error() (line 367) and returns `-1` (line 368) and returns `-1`, so the rest of _modbus_rtu_pre_check_confirmation() is skipped.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: modbus_send_raw_request_tid() drops it when `raw_req_length < 2 || raw_req_length > (MODBUS_MAX_PDU_LENGTH + 1)` (src/modbus.c:244); modbus_proxy() drops it when `req == NULL || req_length < 1` (src/modbus.c:1327); modbus_reply() drops it when `ctx == NULL || req == NULL || mb_mapping == NULL` (src/modbus.c:817).
modbus_read_registers() (src/modbus.c:1596) — Reads the holding registers of remote device and put the data into an array.

Step by step, it checks `ctx == NULL || dest == NULL` (line 1600); if true it calls __error() and returns `-1` straight away; then it checks `nb < 1 || nb > MODBUS_MAX_READ_REGISTERS` (MODBUS_MAX_READ_REGISTERS = 125) (line 1605); if true it calls fprintf(), __error() and returns `-1` straight away; then it checks `ctx->debug` (line 1606); if true it calls fprintf(); then it calls read_registers() and stores the result in `status` (line 1616); then it returns `status` (line 1617).

It is called by main() at tests/bandwidth-client.c:135, only when `modbus_connect(ctx) == -1` is false, repeatedly inside `for (i = 0; i < n_loop; i++)`; main() at tests/proxy-test-client.c:233, only when `ctx == NULL` is false, only when `modbus_connect(ctx) == -1` is false; main() at tests/random-test-client.c:152, repeatedly inside `while (nb_loop++ < LOOP)`, repeatedly inside `for (addr = ADDRESS_START; addr < ADDRESS_END; addr++)`, only when `rc != 1` is false; main() at tests/random-test-client.c:178, repeatedly inside `while (nb_loop++ < LOOP)`, repeatedly inside `for (addr = ADDRESS_START; addr < ADDRESS_END; addr++)`, only when `rc != nb` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → modbus_read_registers().

results.q: What does modbus_read_registers return when too many registers are requested?
answer: The capacity check is in modbus_read_registers() (src/modbus.c:1605): `nb < 1 || nb > MODBUS_MAX_READ_REGISTERS`. When there is not enough, that condition is false and the block at lines 1605–1614 is skipped, so `status` keeps the value it was given at line 1616 (`read_registers(ctx, MODBUS_FC_READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS, addr, nb, dest)`), and modbus_read_registers() returns `read_registers(ctx, MODBUS_FC_READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS, addr, nb, dest)` (line 1617).

results.q: How is a request sent over the serial line?
answer: The best match is modbus_send_raw_request_tid() (src/modbus.c:230).
modbus_send_raw_request_tid() (src/modbus.c:230).

Step by step, it checks `ctx == NULL || raw_req == NULL` (line 239); if true it calls __error() and returns `-1` straight away; then it checks `raw_req_length < 2 || raw_req_length > (MODBUS_MAX_PDU_LENGTH + 1)` (MODBUS_MAX_PDU_LENGTH = 253) (line 244); if true it calls __error() and returns `-1` straight away; then it updates sft (slave, function, t_id; lines 252–255); then it calls one of _modbus_rtu_build_response_basis(), _modbus_tcp_build_response_basis() through _modbus_backend.build_response_basis — which one depends on the data at run time (line 257); then it checks `raw_req_length > 2` (line 259); if true it calls memcpy() and sets `req_length += raw_req_length - 2`; then it calls send_msg() (line 265); then it returns `send_msg(ctx, req, req_length)` (line 265).

It is called by modbus_send_raw_request() at src/modbus.c:270 with (`ctx`, `raw_req`, `raw_req_length`, `0`); modbus_proxy() at src/modbus.c:1370 with (`backend_ctx`, `backend_req`, `backend_req_length`, `0`) — `uint8_t backend_req[MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH]` (line 1314); `backend_req_length = pdu_length + 1` (line 1358), only when `req == NULL || req_length < 1` is false, only when `pdu_length < 1 || pdu_length > MODBUS_MAX_PDU_LENGTH + 1` is false (MODBUS_MAX_PDU_LENGTH = 253), only when `rc == -1` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → modbus_proxy() → modbus_send_raw_request_tid().

The values it updates are used later by _modbus_tcp_build_response_basis() (uses _sft.function, _sft.slave, _sft.t_id); _modbus_rtu_build_response_basis() (uses _sft.function, _sft.slave); modbus_proxy() (uses _sft.function, _sft.slave); response_exception() (uses _sft.function).
Other candidates: modbus_send_raw_request() (src/modbus.c:268), modbus_mask_write_register() (src/modbus.c:1810), write_single() (src/modbus.c:1648).
_modbus_backend.select is a field of type `int (*)(modbus_t *, fd_set *, struct timeval *, int)`, defined in src/modbus-private.h:92.
Nothing in this code assigns _modbus_backend.select after its declaration.
It is read by _modbus_receive_msg() (line 429).
_modbus_backend.select holds a function: at run time it points to _modbus_rtu_select(), _modbus_tcp_select(); it is called by _modbus_receive_msg().
In short: _modbus_backend.select carries a value and consumed by _modbus_receive_msg().
table_crc_hi is a global variable of type `const uint8_t[256]`, defined in src/modbus-rtu.c:33 — the code describes it as: "Table of CRC values for high-order byte".
Nothing in this code assigns table_crc_hi after its declaration.
It is read by crc16() (line 128).
Following where its value goes: table_crc_hi → crc16() → _modbus_rtu_check_integrity() → fprintf() — so it ultimately influences fprintf(), which is an output (file/console log).
In short: table_crc_hi carries a value and consumed by crc16(), feeding fprintf().
